calls.reason: The only evidence is Anthropic's S-1. Its total compute cost fell from 144% to 72% of revenue between Q4 2025 and Q1 2026, which cuts against linear scaling, but that covers one provider and a measure broader than serving cost.
Accenture and Microsoft cut staff token allowances, but no evidence shows a cascade of companies copying them, and the forecast has no deadline.
No record measures the 70% share for the three hyperscalers. Epoch's 15–20% estimate uses a different base, and the funding announcements can't be matched to the $54B and $28B windows.
The S-1 shows a company-wide 2025 net loss but only one reporting segment, so consumer and enterprise losses can't be checked separately. The quality claims have no measure.
No source totals cumulative generative-AI spending through May 2026. Stanford's investment figures and Gartner's forecast measure other things, and 'most wasteful' is rhetoric.
Microsoft's commercial backlog grew 26% excluding OpenAI. Alphabet credits core GCP for part of its 63% cloud growth, and Search grew 19%, so revenue outside the labs was clearly growing.
